Case study: FMEA risk on a pilot submission

Source: vignettes/case-study-fmea-pilot.Rmd
case-study-fmea-pilot.Rmd

A risk log that only lists risks is a to-do list. What a reviewer wants to see is that the risks were ranked, worked, and reduced. r4subrisk puts numbers on that story using a Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA) model: every risk gets a probability, an impact, and a detectability score, and their product is the Risk Priority Number (RPN).

This case study runs the example submission risk register from r4subdata through that model, then shows what happens when the team starts mitigating.

library(r4subrisk)
library(r4subdata)

The register

risk_register_pharma is a worked submission risk log: 18 risks across data quality, traceability, and documentation, each already scored on the three FMEA dimensions.

risk_register_pharma[, c("risk_id", "category", "probability", "impact",
                         "detectability")]
#> # A tibble: 18 × 5
#>    risk_id  category      probability impact detectability
#>    <chr>    <chr>               <int>  <int>         <int>

create_risk_register() validates the scales and computes the RPN and risk level for each row.

rr <- create_risk_register(risk_register_pharma)
rr

The risk picture

compute_risk_scores() rolls the register up: the mean and maximum RPN, an overall 0 to 1 risk score, and the spread of risk levels.

scores <- compute_risk_scores(rr)
scores
#> ℹ Risk Score Summary
#> ℹ   Overall risk score: 0.1982 (0=none, 1=max)
#> ℹ   Mean RPN: 24.8, Max RPN: 48
#> ℹ   Total risks: 18
#> ℹ     high: 3
#> ℹ     low: 4
#> ℹ     medium: 11
scores$category_summary
#> # A tibble: 5 × 3
#>   category          n mean_rpn
#>   <chr>         <int>    <dbl>
#> 1 compliance        4     22.5
#> 2 data_quality      6     25.2
#> 3 documentation     4     18.2
#> 4 programming       2     24  
#> 5 traceability      2     42

The category summary is where prioritisation starts. The categories carrying the highest mean RPN are the ones to work first.

Working the highest risks

Mitigation is the point of the exercise. Suppose the team addresses the two highest-RPN risks: they add the missing SDTM variables and document the ADaM derivation, which lowers both the probability and the detectability difficulty.

ranked <- rr[order(-rr$rpn), c("risk_id", "description", "rpn", "risk_level")]
head(ranked, 3)
#> Warning: Unknown or uninitialised column: `status`.
#> ℹ Risk Register: 3 risk(s), 0 open
#> ℹ   Critical: 0, High: 3, Mean RPN: 48
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>   risk_id  description                                           rpn risk_level
#>   <chr>    <chr>                                               <dbl> <chr>     
#> 1 RISK-006 Laboratory units not standardized across sites         48 high      
#> 2 RISK-008 Traceability gap: ADLB.BASE derivation undocumented    48 high      
#> 3 RISK-013 Incomplete audit trail for manual data corrections     48 high

apply_mitigations() takes the updates and recomputes the RPNs and levels.

top_two <- head(ranked$risk_id, 2)

updates <- data.frame(
  risk_id       = top_two,
  probability   = c(1, 2),
  detectability = c(1, 1),
  status        = "mitigated",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

rr_after <- apply_mitigations(rr, updates)

Before and after

compare_risk_registers() reports what moved: which RPNs dropped, which risk levels changed, and the shift in the mean.

comparison <- compare_risk_registers(rr, rr_after)
comparison$rpn_changes[comparison$rpn_changes$rpn_delta != 0, ]
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   risk_id  rpn_before rpn_after rpn_delta
#>   <chr>         <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 RISK-006         48         4       -44
#> 2 RISK-008         48         6       -42
comparison$delta_mean_rpn
#> [1] -4.8

The mean RPN falls and the two worked risks drop to lower levels. That is the before-and-after a reviewer is looking for: not that the study had no risks, but that the risks were found, ranked, and brought down.

Feeding the readiness score

The risk register does not live in isolation. risk_register_to_evidence() turns it into R4SUB evidence rows, which flow into the Risk pillar of the Submission Confidence Index alongside quality, trace, and usability evidence. The FMEA work you do here shows up directly in the submission’s readiness score.
